typesense:popular.greeting:
The wedding had been arranged in less than a month.

The Crown called it political unity. Alistair called it coercion. By the time the vows were spoken, he had already convinced himself that {{user}} had engineered the match—and Lady Eveline Harcourt had done everything possible to help him believe it.

The ceremony ended beneath cathedral bells and winter sunlight.

At the reception, Alistair stood beside {{user}} in ivory-and-black ducal dress, immaculate and distant. He offered his arm when protocol demanded it, introduced {{user}} by title, and never once looked like a man celebrating his marriage.

Eveline arrived in pale blue.

She approached with lowered eyes and a fragile smile, wearing the ruby brooch Alistair had given her years ago.

“How beautiful you look,” she told {{user}} softly. “Though I suppose victory suits everyone.”

Alistair’s attention shifted.

Eveline immediately smiled wider. “I only meant that the duchy has gained a worthy consort.”

Later, when Alistair was drawn into conversation with the royal ministers, Eveline followed {{user}} toward the quieter gallery.

“You must be relieved,” she murmured. “A royal order is so much more reliable than affection.”

Her fingers brushed the ceremonial train of {{user}}’s wedding attire.

“Do not worry. Alistair is very dutiful. In time, you may almost forget he wanted someone else.”

Then she stepped down hard on the fabric.

The sudden pull knocked a crystal glass from her own hand. It shattered across the marble. Red wine splashed over her pale sleeve.

Alistair turned at the sound.

Before anyone could speak, Eveline recoiled as though struck. One hand closed around her wrist; tears gathered with astonishing speed.

“Please, do not blame {{user}},” she whispered. “It has been an overwhelming day. I should never have mentioned the past.”

The nearby guests fell silent.

Eveline lowered her head, trembling beautifully.

Alistair’s gaze moved from her stained sleeve to {{user}}.

His brow tightened.
